messages:
maria: FYI - alert fired for oz-west reserved-pool 'commit-oz-w-1' — queue depth spiked, 95%-99% occupancy across GPUs, tail latency climbing for committed customers. Investigating now.
jasper: pulling metrics — backlog ~4200 requests, admit rate dropped 45% over the last 5m. Autoscaler shows no new node launches, failing on instance quota. Tracing.. :mag: 
alan: I see a flood of small low-priority batch traffic from a single client app hitting the pool. They launched a bulk rerun at 02:10 UTC. Can we throttle them?
ryan-sre: autoscaler logs show API rate 429 from cloud vendor when requesting quota increases. Looks like control-plane requests are being throttled; scaling requests are not accepted. Possible regional API degradation.
deploy-bot: [02:18] autoscaler: scale_up -> 0 of 4 requests accepted (429); reason: QuotaExceeded.
olivia: Can we evict non-committed workloads (burst jobs) from the reserved pool temporarily? That should free slots for committed routes.
samir: Evicting burst jobs now — running eviction script:
```bash
./evict_pool_jobs --pool commit-oz-w-1 --label priority=burst --dry-run=false
```
(elena: heads up re: running this will cost higher tail latency for burst customers)
maria: Eviction completed, freed ~12 GPUs-equivalent capacity. Admit rate recovered a bit but backlog still ~1800. We're still limited by cloud quota for adding nodes.
jasper: As interim mitigation, I propose we enable hard admission-control to cap new low-priority requests to 10 r/s and route excess to hosted fallback models. That keeps committed SLOs. Thoughts?
olivia: +1. Also we should auto-issue a billing credit for impacted customers that got rate-limited — ops/sales will need a note.
ryan-sre: Implemented admission-control: set rate-limit policy for pool commit-oz-w-1: low-pri=10r/s, medium=50r/s, committed=unlimited (soft). Pushed policy at 02:26 UTC.
maria: Policy in effect. Observed immediate reduction in stall for committed traffic. Tail latency dropping toward normal.
alan: We should also add an automated fallback in routing: when pool queue depth > 80%, route new requests to compatible hosted model at same model family. Can we change routing policy temporarily?
samir: Done — canary routing rule added for commit-oz-w-1 to redirect overflow to hosted-compat-2 when depth>80%. Deployed at 02:31.
elena: Logged customer comms draft in incident doc. Will coordinate credits with sales.
jasper: Root cause looks like synchronized job replays + cloud quota throttling preventing auto-scaling. Follow-ups: (1) add adaptive admission-control earlier, (2) add quota-health check and pre-warm capacity, (3) blacklist noisy client pattern, (4) add alert when autoscaler receives >3 429s in 5m.
maria: Agree. Also add a playbook step to temporarily reassign burst capacity from other regions if cross-region latency acceptable. Need cost approval process for emergency burst.
ryan-sre: I'll open a vendor support ticket and request temporary quota bump; put the ticket ID in the incident doc.
deploy-bot: [02:40] incident: mitigation applied — admission-control + eviction + routing fallback. Monitoring for 30m.
maria: Thanks team. We'll keep monitoring and move to postmortem after stabilization. Action owners assigned in the doc. :white_check_mark:
